mechanism: Autonomic neuropathy + chronic hyperglycemia produce pathological glucose-HR hyper-coupling.
statement: Legacy analysis reports awake glucose-HR correlation increases monotonically across healthy(-0.041)->pre-diabetes(-0.010)->oral(0.015)->insulin(0.045), Cohen's d=0.585, FDR p=1.3e-19, surviving full confounder adjustment.

mechanism: Insulin resistance reduces activity-driven glucose uptake, weakening negative glucose-activity coupling.
statement: Legacy analysis reports glucose-activity Spearman correlation becomes less negative with diabetes severity, Cohen's d=0.475, FDR p=1.04e-14; effect attenuated but survives full adjustment (FDR=8.22e-07).
Legacy analysis reports coupling-only features classify healthy vs insulin-dependent at AUROC=0.805; combined coupling+raw AUROC=0.952; coupling-only HbA1c prediction R2=0.144 vs combined 0.674.

Legacy analysis reports coupling features associate with systemic burden after age/site adjustment: glucose-HR vs frailty partial r=0.148 (FDR=2.18e-09); glucose MSE vs allostatic load r=0.130; glucose-activity vs homeostatic dysregulation r=0.151.

mechanism: Impaired fast parasympathetic buffering reduces short-scale coherence while metabolic/hormonal coupling at 2-8h strengthens.
statement: Legacy analysis reports glucose-HR coupling is timescale-selective: broadband d=0.06 (n.s.), short periods 30-60min/1-2h DECREASE (d=-0.22/-0.17), long periods 2-4h/4-8h INCREASE (d=+0.33/+0.38, FDR p=1e-8); directionality flips near 2h.
